29.0.1.en: It specifies the requirements for the day of the ordination of the priests and their consecration to the priestly work, which God commanded Moses to prepare, and they are:

29.0.2.en: 1- The bullock: offered as a sin offering.

29.0.3.en: 2- A ram as a burnt offering.

29.0.4.en: 3- Another ram as an offering of consecration.

29.0.5.en: These sacrifices signify Christ, who offers Himself for us on the Cross and sheds His blood for us, and by His blood gives the Church her Holy Sacraments, among them the sacrament of the priesthood.

29.1.0.en: Besides the sacrifices, Moses prepares a vegetable offering consisting of doughs made of the finest kind of flour, which is wheat, and they signify the life of Christ on earth, which is without blemish. The offering includes three kinds:-

29.1.1.en: 1- Unleavened bread, that is, without leaven, because leaven signifies the evil that spreads inside a person, as Christ spoke of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is their hypocrisy (Lk 12:1).

29.1.2.en: 2- Cakes unleavened, tempered with oil, that is, kneaded with oil. We note here the addition of oil, which signifies the work of the Holy Spirit.

29.1.3.en: 3- Wafers unleavened anointed with oil, which are like the previous cakes but thinner than they.

29.1.4.en: In the three previous kinds the variety is to be noted, and what is meant by it is the variety of virtues in the life of Christ and in the life of the priest consecrated to God.

29.2.0.en: The kinds of bread mentioned above are put in one basket, because they signify the life of the one Christ who redeems all humanity and the priest who prays for all his people. The sacrifices and the basket are offered before God on the day of the ordination of the priests.

29.2.1.en: Take care to prepare everything that the service needs so that it may be complete before God, and take more care to prepare yourself for prayer by driving away every evil thought and remembering the greatness of being before God. Reading the Holy Bible, examining yourself or repeating a hymn ... etc. helps you in this. This makes you feel the presence of God and enjoy the depth of the words of prayer.

29.3.s.en: (2) The steps of consecrating the priests

29.3.0.en: The first step in consecrating the priests is washing them with water, that is, a complete bath, and this was in the laver set up inside the tent of meeting before entering the Holy Place. It signifies purity from every sin and the rejection of evil. This rite is still performed in the Divine Liturgy by the priest washing his hands before beginning it.

29.4.0.en: The second step is putting on the priestly garments. He first puts on the coat and ties it with a girdle at the waist, then puts on the robe, and after that puts the ephod over it and ties it with the girdle at the waist, and puts the breastplate on his breast, in which are the Urim and the Thummim, then puts on the mitre, and on it the crown, that is, the gold plate on which is written Holiness to the Lord. These garments that the high priest wears signify putting on righteousness and a good life with God, and his bearing the responsibility of caring for his people, who are on his breast and on his shoulder, as we mentioned in

29.5.0.en: The third step is anointing with oil, which is a mixture of sweet-smelling materials blended with oil, as will be mentioned in (ch. 30), and it is also called the oil of gladness (Ps 45:7) and "the precious ointment" (Ps 133:2). The anointing is done by pouring the oil on the head of Aaron, in addition to anointing him and his garments with oil. The oil signifies the Holy Spirit, who descends on the priest and works in him and gives him the power to carry out the service of the priesthood, and which became a sacrament of the Church in the New Testament. The anointing with sweet oil also signifies:

29.5.1.en: 1- That the priests are the sweet fragrance to God before and in the midst of their people.

29.5.2.en: 2- Just as oil is used for lighting, the priests give light and are a light in the midst of their people.

29.5.3.en: 3- The anointing of the priests in the Old Testament signifies Christ, who was anointed with the Holy Spirit to accomplish our redemption (Lk 4:

29.6.0.en: "Gird bonnets on them": that is, put bonnets on them.

29.6.1.en: As for the priests, Moses clothes them in their priestly garments, which are fewer than the garments of Aaron the high priest. They put on coats and tie them with a girdle at the waist, then bonnets on their heads, which were most probably a cap around which a piece of cloth is wound, like the winding of a turban among some people. They are anointed with oil, but oil is not poured on their heads, for this distinguishes the high priest to proclaim that he is the head of the priesthood.

29.6.2.en: "Consecrating them" means their being filled with the grace of God to exercise the priesthood, and also they take of the sacrifice of consecration and eat of it, and this signifies the spiritual satisfaction that the priest receives, for he is satisfied spiritually and materially and lacks nothing.

29.6.3.en: Filling the hand also means sharing in offering the sacrifice by carrying a part of it and moving it before God, that is, beginning the priestly service. That is, filling the hand is the sanctification of the priests, that is, setting them apart for the priestly service and their beginning in it.

29.6.4.en: The service of God is very great, so if you approach it in any work, even a small one, take care to repent of every sin and to adorn yourself with the virtues that the Holy Spirit helps you to acquire, and you will be able to experience the work of God in the service and rejoice in it.

29.7.0.en: The consecration, that is, the ordination of these priests, is done by the hand of Moses, who signifies the bishop or the Patriarch, before the tent of meeting, which signifies the Church, that is, they are ordained before God and before His people. Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the head of the bullock so that their sins are transferred from their heads. It is a symbol of the sacrament of confession, where the sin is transferred from the head of the penitent to Christ, who was slain for us on the Cross.

29.8.0.en: This bullock is a sin offering and it signifies the sacrifice of the Cross in one of its aspects, and it bears the sins of men, among them the priests, because he too is a man liable to fall into sin, so it is slain before the tent of meeting, proclaiming that salvation is in the Church.

29.9.0.en: The blood is gathered in basins as before, which are called pans, that is, flat vessels (ch. 27:3), and Moses takes some of it and puts it on the horns of the altar, which signify strength, that is, the sacrifice of Christ is strong and offers complete forgiveness to whoever believes in Him, confesses his sins and approaches the sacrament of the priesthood.

29.9.1.en: The rest of the blood he pours at the bottom of the altar, and perhaps what is meant is that the blood falls into the compass, which is like a concave shelf at the middle of the altar, so that the blood does not fall on the ground (ch. 27:5). The anointing of the altar with blood is done to sanctify it because of the sins of the people that defile it and anger God (v. 36, Lev 8:15, 16:16). And because the life of the animal is in its blood, pouring it at the bottom of the altar is a declaration by man that the blood of the animal makes atonement for him instead of the death of man himself, and this signifies the blood of Christ, who died for us and redeemed us.

29.10.0.en: The fat is the richest thing inside the body of the animal, so it is always offered to God and burned on the altar, with part of the liver and the two kidneys because of their importance as well. It is understood from this that the animal is cut open and its inside exposed, and this signifies a person's examining his thoughts and the intentions of his heart and everything inside him.

29.10.1.en: May you examine yourself every day before God and offer repentance for all your sins, even if they are in thought or intention, so that you are purified and the words of prayer and praise take their place, and you become a sacrifice of love before Him, like the fat that is burned on the altar.

29.11.0.en: His dung: the waste of the bullock that is inside its digestive system.

29.11.1.en: The rest of the animal, that is, its flesh, its skin and its dung, is burned outside the camp, that is, the place where the children of Israel dwell, as a symbol of God's aversion to sin. This bullock is a sin offering, so it is burned far from God, who hates sin. The sin offering signifies Christ, who bore our sins and died for us on the Cross outside the camp, that is, outside Jerusalem.

29.12.0.en: Moses takes one of the two rams, and Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head, proclaiming that this ram will stand in their place before God. It signifies Christ, who was offered for us on the Cross and pleased God by His pure life, so God is pleased with us if we believe in Him and live with Him.

29.13.0.en: The ram is slain to be offered as a burnt offering before God, as a symbol of Christ, who is without sin and died for us, that the Father might smell a sweet savour on our behalf, and the blood of the ram is sprinkled on the four sides of the bronze altar, so it flows and gathers in the compass, that is, the shelf below the surface of the altar.

29.14.0.en: He takes care to cut the ram into pieces, as a symbol of the sufferings of Christ that He passed through throughout His life, and these pieces and all its inside are washed, proclaiming its purity outwardly and inwardly, for it signifies the righteous Christ, who died for us to be a sweet savour before God. This points to the importance of the priest's purity inwardly and outwardly, that is, in his conduct and his thoughts.

29.14.1.en: Accept pain and weariness for the sake of God, and endure insults and false accusations with purity of heart and without agitation, and you will become a sacrifice of love and a sweet savour before God.

29.15.0.en: The flesh of the animal and everything in it is burned on the altar as a burnt offering to please God.

29.16.0.en: The second ram is offered as an offering of consecration, that is, a sacrifice from which they fill their hands and with which they begin to practice the sacrament of the priesthood (Lev 8:22), and they take of it to eat, to proclaim a fellowship of love between them and God. Therefore Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the sacrifice to proclaim their love for God, and He in His love gives them of it to eat, so that they share with Him in one feeling of love.

29.17.0.en: After the ram is slain, Moses takes some of the blood and touches the tip of the ear of Aaron and of his sons, which is the soft lower part of the flesh of the ear, and it signifies the sanctification of the ear to hear the word of God. He also touches the thumb of the right hand, which is the most important finger of the hand, as a symbol of the sanctification of the works of the priests and their consecration to God. Then he touches the great toe of the right foot, which is the most important toe of the foot, as a symbol of the sanctification of their conduct and all their ways to God. The right members were chosen because they signify strength and blessing, and these members represent the whole man. The blood is sprinkled on the four sides of the altar, like the rite of the burnt offering.

29.18.0.en: After that he sprinkles some of the blood on the priests and their garments, as a symbol that their priesthood is taken from the blood of Christ, then he sprinkles some of the anointing oil, which proclaims their consecration to the service of the Lord. The blood signifies the covenant between God and the priests, and the anointing with oil signifies the grace of the Holy Spirit given to them to perform their service.

29.19.0.en: The rump: the tail of the sheep, full of fat.

29.19.1.en: The offering of consecration is a kind of peace offering in which the one who offers it shares in eating of it, and the offering of consecration is offered only on the day of the priest's ordination, because it is a proclamation of the beginning of his service and its being handed over to him. In this sacrifice Moses takes all the fat that is in the sacrifice with part of the liver and the two kidneys and offers it on the altar to God to be burned, as is the custom in all the sacrifices, because God first takes the richest and most important part of the sacrifice, and to it is added the right shoulder of the ram, which is what the priest takes from the sacrifices of the people. Here, however, because the sacrifice is offered on behalf of the priest, God takes the right shoulder to be burned on the altar, and it signifies works, for the right hand signifies strength, so strong works are offered to God before man uses his strength for his own needs.

29.20.0.en: To what is offered to God of the offering of consecration is added a sample of each of the material offerings, because when God takes of the offering He blesses the rest of the food when the priests eat it.

29.20.1.en: Be careful to offer to God the firstfruits of your time and your abilities, to proclaim your love for Him, and He will bless the rest of your works and thoughts, and you will always enjoy His fellowship.

29.21.0.en: Moses places the fat, the right shoulder and the material offerings on the hands of Aaron and his sons, to proclaim that they are the ones who offer them before the Lord with pleasure and joy. Waving means a horizontal movement of the hand forward, then backward, then right and after that left, so they offer the offering to God, who is glorified in the four directions of the world. They offer it forward toward the altar, that is, God, then backward, that is, toward themselves, and so they receive a blessing by offering this sacrifice, then they move their hands right and left, that is, the whole people whom they shepherd receive a blessing from their priestly service.

29.22.0.en: All these parts of the ram of consecration, with the vegetable offerings, that is, the unleavened bread, the tempered cakes and the wafers, are offered to God as a sacrifice of love, and Moses burns them on the altar.

29.23.0.en: The ram of consecration, which is Aaron's: that is, the ram offered for the consecration of Aaron and his sons.

29.23.1.en: The breast: the bone to which the chest of the sacrifice is attached, containing the greatest amount of flesh and the finest.

29.23.2.en: The breast, or chest of the sacrifice, Moses carries on his hands and waves, that is, lifts up, because it is offered to God who dwells in heaven, and brings it down, that is, it is given as a gift from God to him, then he takes it to cook it and eat it, he and his household. This is a proclamation of the blessing that the priest receives from his service, which he takes here in material form as a part of the sacrifice, and it also signifies the spiritual blessings that the priest of the New Testament receives from his service.

29.24.0.en: Heave offering: the sacrifice or offering that is lifted up to God who dwells in heaven, that is, offered to Him.

29.24.1.en: God declares here to Moses that the priest's portion of the sacrifices that the people offer is the breast, or chest, of the sacrifice and the right shoulder, and he takes them as food for himself and his household from the peace offerings. As for this sacrifice offered on the day of Aaron's ordination, Moses took the breast, but throughout their days the priest takes the breast from the sacrifices of the people.

29.24.2.en: Take care to offer your love to God, whether in holy worship or in service to Him, for it is a blessing to you, in addition to its gladdening the heart of God, who pours out His mercies on you, setting before your eyes His love that He offered to you on the Cross, that you may respond to it with what you offer to Him.

29.25.0.en: The priestly garments that were sanctified by the anointing of Aaron the high priest are worn by the one who is appointed high priest after his death, in order to sanctify these great garments because they entered before God and His service.

29.25.1.en: How great it is to enter before God, and greater than it is to partake of His Holy Mysteries. So take care for the day of your partaking of the Holy Mysteries and enjoy entering the Church, that is, into the presence of God. Indeed, it is also possible for you to enjoy it whether in your chamber or in any place, so that not only your garments but your heart also becomes holy.

29.26.0.en: The rite of consecrating the priests or the high priest is that he remain in these garments seven days inside the tent of meeting, to enjoy the presence of God and be filled with His grace at the beginning of his service, as is mentioned in detail in (Lev 8:33-35). In the New Testament the new priest enjoys a retreat of 40 days in the monastery.

29.27.s.en: (7) The food of the priests and the consecration of the altar

29.27.0.en: After the fat and the right shoulder are burned on the altar and Moses takes the breast or chest, the priests take the rest of the flesh of the ram and cook it beside the door of the tent of meeting, that is, they do not leave the tent of meeting.

29.28.0.en: Those with which the atonement was made: that is, Aaron and his sons, for whom it was offered.

29.28.1.en: A stranger: one who is not of the priests.

29.28.2.en: Aaron and his sons, that is, all the priests, eat of the flesh of the ram because it is an atoning sacrifice for them, and this is at the door of the tent of meeting because they are guests of God, so they are sanctified and consecrated to the service of God. This eating means making a covenant with God that they be consecrated to His service, and He is responsible for them and provides for their spiritual and material needs, in addition to the priests' doing all their works before God, that is, pleasing Him. This is a symbol of the atoning sacrifice of Christ for His priests in the sacrament of the priesthood and its power given in this sacrament.

29.29.0.en: The offering of consecration, like the peace offering, is eaten of by the one who offers it, and it signifies the sacrifice of the New Testament, that is, the Body and Blood of the Lord. Out of sanctification of it nothing of it remains to the next day, and if any remains it is burned, because if anything of the offering of consecration remained it would be liable to corruption or someone other than the priests might eat of it and sin. It is not eaten on the next day because it is holy, that is, set apart for the priests, so they eat it on the day of their consecration.

29.29.1.en: The ram of consecration also signifies Christ, who was slain on the Cross to consecrate priests for the service of His people and that they may be stewards of His mysteries.

29.30.0.en: What was done on the first day for the consecration of the priests is repeated, which is offering a bullock and two rams for seven days, and these offerings are offered daily. This is to confirm the holiness of the priesthood and so that the priest may remain inside the tent of meeting, as the priest of the New Testament remains 40 days in the monastery after his ordination.

29.31.0.en: Most holy: the bronze altar becomes holy, equal to the Holy of Holies.

29.31.1.en: These sacrifices, that is, the bullock and the two rams, which are offered daily, sanctify and consecrate not only the priests but the bronze altar also, so the altar becomes holy and sanctifies and blesses whoever touches it.

29.31.2.en: The sacrament of Holy Communion sanctifies your life and consecrates your heart to God, so be careful to practice it throughout the year and before great undertakings, that He may bless you in your life.

29.32.0.en: Of the first year: that is, a year old, a reference to complete growth and maturity and at the same time to innocence and purity.

29.32.1.en: After the ordination of the priests, God spoke to them about the daily burnt offerings that the priests would offer to Him immediately after their ordination, which are two lambs of the first year, one a morning burnt offering and the other an evening burnt offering. On the bronze altar a lamb one year old is offered in the morning as a burnt offering to please God, and before its fire goes out, between the two evenings, that is, between three and five in the afternoon, another burnt offering is offered, so that a fire always remains burning on the altar. This fire came down from heaven the first time and then remained burning on the altar throughout the years by these burnt offerings, besides the various burnt offerings of the people.

29.33.0.en: A tenth deal: that is, a tenth of an ephah, and the ephah equals 23 liters, so its tenth equals 2.3 liters.

29.33.1.en: The hin: equals 3.8 liters, and its fourth part equals about a liter.

29.33.2.en: Beaten oil: olive oil pressed by beating, not by crushing, and the former is purer.

29.33.3.en: With the morning or evening burnt offering is offered a tenth of an ephah of flour kneaded with a fourth part of a hin of oil. The flour and the oil represent the fruits of the earth, and of them is offered to God that He may afterward bless the food of His people. The flour also signifies the holy offering, while the oil signifies the Holy Spirit.

29.33.4.en: A fourth part of a hin of wine is also poured on the sacrifice. Wine too is of the fruits of the earth, that God may bless the harvest of the grapes and the wine of His people.

29.33.5.en: In the New Testament the wine is changed into the Blood of Christ, so the pouring out of wine signifies the sacrifice of the New Testament.

29.33.6.en: How beautiful it is to offer to God of your money and possessions for the Church and the needy, for God blesses all that you have until it is more than you need and you feel rest and peace in your heart.

29.34.0.en: An evening burnt offering is also offered, like the morning one, gladdening the heart of God, for it shows His people's love for Him in their holy worship.

29.35.0.en: At the door of the tent of meeting: that is, on the bronze altar that is in front of the door of the tent.

29.35.1.en: The offering of these burnt offerings continues throughout life on the bronze altar near the door of the tent of meeting, and there God speaks with Moses and his allies of the priests and prophets and makes clear to His people how they are to live with Him. These sacrifices continued to be offered throughout the Old Testament as evidence of the insufficiency of the sacrifice to satisfy God, for it was merely a symbol of the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross, which He offered once and which atoned for all humanity who believe in Him.

29.36.0.en: When God appears in the form of a cloud before the tent of meeting, He blesses His people and sanctifies them and cleanses them.

29.37.0.en: God promises to sanctify the tent of meeting and the priests if they offer the previous sacrifices in this chapter.

29.38.0.en: How beautiful are the feelings of God, who wishes to restore the life of the first Paradise, so that as He was with Adam and Eve He may be with His people and in their midst to bless them always.

29.39.0.en: When the people see God dwelling in the cloud before them, they feel His greatness and His power which brought them out of the land of Egypt, and they remain firm in faith in Him.

29.39.1.en: The altar of incense, the laver, the composition of the oil and incense, and the silver of the ransom
